question.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4{(\frac{2}{7})}^{x-1}-8 & \le 0 \\ 4{(\frac{2}{7})}^{x-1} & \le 8 \\ {(\frac{2}{7})}^{x-1} & \le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{2}{7})}^{x-1}] & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ (x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{7}) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ (x-1)(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡7) & \le \operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, note that $\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡7$ is a negative quantity, so when we divide both sides by it, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & \ge \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡7} \\ x & \ge \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}+1\end{aligned}
$$
